title: Bix's influence on Chicago came through records
summary: Ashcraft and Steiner discuss Bix at Lake Forest and his friend Cy Welge, and whether they knew the New Orleans Rhythm Kings before hearing the record.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Maybe a little later, before he arrived in Chicago.
Well, I think he was in Lake Forest in 21.

And also, it's hard for people to realize that Bix, Bix's influence on Chicago was almost entirely through records, because he generally played in Indiana. He very rarely played around Chicago. Cy Welge was his great friend at Lake Forest and a drummer. And they played together a little bit, jobbing dates.
Before he had developed a style or maybe a... Yes. Before he had heard many things.
Except the record you talked about.
Well, the Farewell Blues record, I remember particularly just because it was the first.
Had you known the New Orleans Rhythm Kings before you heard this record? No. You've never been to hear them?
No. I'd heard about them, but I hadn't heard them at all.
That, of course, was a Jeanette, and it was the first of a series that they made.
